scope: Thirty new production DSP responsiveness/render-speed costs after the prior 74 implemented opportunities and both rounds of 100; startup, unchanged helpers, bug fixes and the same cost at multiple callsites are excluded.
runtimeClosure: Existing application DSP files only. No native StaffPad/WASM bytes, assistance source recipes/pins/archive inventories, dependency metadata or native runtime target changes. No new production module or desktop runtime inventory entry.

parity.provenance: Independent esbuild bundle captured before production edits, /tmp/perf300-dsp-baseline/fixtures.mjs; fixtures exercise public production APIs for exact typed-array bytes, doubles/signed zero, snapshots and painted geometry. Three admitted overridden-length spectrum cases were added by invoking the same frozen original spectrum export; all 166 hashes match.
parity.additionalLoudnessValidation: The earlier 15-test EBU group also passed, including the 11 existing loudness/audit cases beyond the four cases overlapping final focused selection.
parity.ownership: Spectrum pooled scratch is private, geometry-bounded and leased under reentrancy/exception. Frequency history copies samples before caller regains control; peak output retains Float32 rounding. Input validation, arbitrary stream partitions, published live telemetry, reset, worker cancellation and returned PCM ownership remain unchanged.
parity.independentReviewStatus: Complete. Independent timeline read audit caught an admitted overridden-length spectrum mismatch; red exact baseline tests now prove corrected native-length guard and original-traversal fallback. The corrected sources passed all193 additional independent baseline comparisons. No remaining correctness defect, dead path or duplicate counted cost was found in the read review.

independentReview.reviewer: timeline agent, independently of the implementation

spectrum.coverage: Own-property and Proxy reported lengths -3, 0, 2, 2.5 and 7; offsets 0, 1, 1.5, 4 and 30; average both false and true. Exact baseline output or thrown behavior was compared.

additionalDsp.coverage: Circular-centroid leading/trailing boundaries, mono/stereo/six channels and irregular chunks; guarded constant Chirp endpoints and partial blocks; EBU reset, standby and true-peak history drain.

measurementMethod: scripts/performance/measure-dsp-responsiveness-round4.ts independently bundles exact baseline/current source closures, checks output digests outside timers and records 12 alternating AB/BA warm pairs per 13 public-kernel jobs, with source SHA256 and host metadata.
measurementLimits: Grouped synchronous kernel timings do not establish per-finding milliseconds, desktop click-to-Apply, startup, first-use latency or sustained FPS. Rejected Chirp closure shapes and their regressions are retained in the receipt; final variable loop is unchanged and short-path/shared-host variance is disclosed.

findings.title: Prepare true-peak FIR ring tap indices
findings.avoidedCost: Replace four phases of twelve per-tap remainder operations with an immutable twelve-position index table.
findings.evidence: A nonzero channel frame previously evaluated 48 tap-index remainders; the same ordered 48 FIR additions now read prepared Uint8 indices.
findings.limitations: Twelve twelve-byte rows; no FIR coefficient or phase/tap addition order changes. Ring head uses its bounded wrap.

findings.title: Skip FIR multiply/add work for exactly zero history
findings.avoidedCost: Track exactly occupied nonzero ring slots; all-zero histories perform no 48-tap interpolation.
findings.evidence: Red/green instrumented production source: 997 signed-zero frames execute zero tap multiplications; an impulse executes 48; after exactly 12 draining frames no further taps run.
findings.limitations: Both signs of zero are stored and the ring index always advances. A single nonzero slot keeps the complete original FIR. Meter reset retains live filter/history behavior; rejected chunks still preflight before mutation.

findings.title: Use bounded loudness-energy ring wraps
findings.avoidedCost: Remove remainder operations from energy expiration and advancement in all three per-frame loudness windows.
findings.evidence: Each full energy window formerly evaluated two remainder operations per frame. Source comparison proves bounded subtract/branch indices address identical slots; exact EBU snapshots cover 8000/11025/48000 Hz.
findings.limitations: Subtraction, insertion and accumulation order are unchanged, including clamping negative residual energy and partial window denominators.

findings.title: Retain unchanged histogram summaries
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid gating and percentile rescans when snapshots are requested without an accepted histogram mutation.
findings.evidence: Red/green: 100 repeated integrated/LRA summaries perform zero bin conversions after the first summary; accepted pushes and reset invalidate; rejected 0/NaN energies retain the result.
findings.limitations: Only private derived numeric results are retained. Every accepted push and reset invalidates both summaries. Running/standby toggles keep histogram semantics.

findings.title: Resolve all four LRA percentile ranks in one traversal
findings.avoidedCost: Replace four independent rank scans with one ordered scan resolving the exact lower/upper ranks for10th and95th percentiles.
findings.evidence: Red/green dense 100-bin fixture resolves all ranks within 100 visited bins instead of repeated traversals; frozen snapshots retain original interpolation and subtraction bytes.
findings.limitations: Rank ordering handles the two-sample crossing case. Each original percentile interpolation retains its arithmetic order; no rank approximation or threshold change.

findings.title: Avoid loudness math for empty gating bins
findings.avoidedCost: Check private occupancy before calculating a bin loudness during gating.
findings.evidence: Red/green sparse histogram with two distant occupied bins performs at most two loudness-bin conversions rather than hundreds.
findings.limitations: Both gates continue scanning identical index bounds and sum occupied counts/energies in original ascending order.

findings.title: Reduce channel true peaks without temporary arrays
findings.avoidedCost: Replace per-snapshot map arrays and argument spreads with an ordered channel maximum.
findings.evidence: Both 10 Hz publication and partial-window snapshot eliminate one channel-sized temporary array/spread each; exact 6-channel snapshots match the baseline.
findings.limitations: Same live peak seed and channel order; no state or output object is reused or exposed.

findings.title: Prepare spectrogram FFT band intervals once per job
findings.avoidedCost: Calculate band start/end/count once outside the column loop instead of for every column.
findings.evidence: Red/green 256-point FFT / 31-band / 64-column test bounds Math.floor calls to fixed geometry plus 64 offsets; former work exceeded the limit due repeated band and half-window geometry.
findings.limitations: Each column still computes every original hypot and adds bins in the original order; interval endpoints and division remain exact.

findings.title: Bound array-backed spectrogram sample loading
findings.avoidedCost: Use one source interval and zero padding per column instead of a boundary branch for each FFT sample.
findings.evidence: For 512 columns of 256 samples, at most 512 bound pairs replace 131072 per-sample boundary checks. Exact array/accessor energy fixtures and all existing spectrogram tests pass.
findings.limitations: Ordinary projected clip worker/accessor inputs retain the full original sampleAt traversal and do not claim this bounds reduction. Actual Soundscaper array input is the recording multiview preview exported by preview.ts to the canvas analysis fallback when analysis is not deferred (including unavailable Worker or width beyond the worker limit). Projected sampleAt accessors still receive every negative/trailing frame request. Fractional array-like lengths retain ceil boundary behavior. Number coercion and invalid sample fallback are unchanged.

findings.title: Prepare inverse spectrogram scale endpoints once per row plan
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid repeating two fixed nonlinear endpoint transformations for every interior raster row.
findings.evidence: Red/green 181-row mel plan performs 5762 log10 calls instead of 6120: two endpoints plus 180 ordered 32-step inversions.
findings.limitations: Existing row-plan cache and its bounds remain unchanged; endpoint clamping and midpoint bisection order are exact.

findings.title: Select the inverse spectrogram scale function once
findings.avoidedCost: Remove per-bisection string scale dispatch by selecting one numeric transformation at plan creation.
findings.evidence: A 181-row nonlinear plan formerly dispatched the selected scale on every 32-step midpoint (5760 times); now one plan-level choice serves all rows. All six painted scale fixtures are exact.
findings.limitations: Number normalization and every scale formula remain unchanged. Small row-plan timings are near host noise; no isolated millisecond gain is asserted.

findings.title: Accumulate rounded frequency bands directly into peaks
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid allocating and writing three full chunk PCM arrays for each visual channel solely to read them back as extrema.
findings.evidence: Red/green stereo 4097-frame analyzer.push allocates zero Float32 arrays instead of six full PCM arrays. Every intermediate band value still passes Math.fround; extrema remain bucket-local.
findings.limitations: Public splitter.process retains owned PCM output and reset. Direct accumulation uses immutable private crossover frequencies and independent channel state; ordinary caller PCM is consumed synchronously and never retained.

findings.title: Share peak bucket geometry across bands and channels
findings.avoidedCost: Calculate one initial peak bucket and integer boundaries once per chunk instead of repeating bucket division for every band/channel span.
findings.evidence: Red/green 511-frame stereo push performs one bucket floor rather than twelve. This is distinct from avoiding full band PCM: it removes repeated bucket interval arithmetic.
findings.limitations: Incomplete bucket extrema retain original Float32 values and sample order. The now-unused public peak helper was restored unchanged and is not counted.

findings.title: Retain centroid FFT input in a circular buffer
findings.avoidedCost: Advance a private circular start instead of copying1792 retained samples per channel at every256-frame hop.
findings.evidence: Red/green analyzer history performs zero Float32.copyWithin calls. Each FFT reads at most two contiguous spans in the same logical order; irregular 1/127/8192-frame fixtures match.
findings.limitations: Leading zero history, final silence padding, centroid Float32 accumulations and FFT input order are preserved. Retained history is private after caller chunk mutation.

findings.title: Avoid clearing centroid slots that will be overwritten
findings.avoidedCost: Remove the256-slot zero fill after each FFT hop; every consumed slot is filled by input or explicit finish silence before the next transform.
findings.evidence: Red/green history test executes zero positive-offset tail fills. This is separate from retained 1792-frame memcpy removal: it avoids the newly writable 256-frame clear.
findings.limitations: Initial typed arrays remain zero initialized; all ring slots consumed by FFT have been written, including final partial chunks and source nonfinite sanitization.

findings.title: Bound integer-offset spectrum PCM loads
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid undefined typed-array probes, finiteness checks and window multiplication for padded tail samples.
findings.evidence: 211-frame input with 8192-bin FFT avoids 7981 sample probes per channel; zero padding is written directly. Fractional-offset fixtures retain their original fallback traversal.
findings.limitations: Bounded loading requires integer source offsets and intrinsic typed-array length equal to declared frameCount. Overridden lengths and admitted proxies retain the original full sample traversal. Channel validation and in-range finite sanitization are unchanged; FFT power addition order is preserved.

findings.title: Reuse bounded private spectrum FFT scratch
findings.avoidedCost: Retain one real/imaginary/power workspace per accepted power-of-two geometry instead of allocating three double arrays for every spectrum request.
findings.evidence: Red/green warmed spectrum allocates zero Float64 arrays rather than three. Reentrant computations lease separate scratch; exceptions release leases; returned frozen bins remain independent.
findings.limitations: At most twelve retained workspaces (2,620,896 bytes, under 3 MiB); recursive leases are ephemeral. No caller PCM or output array is pooled; power buffers are cleared on each reuse.

findings.title: Calculate crossover feedback once per frame
findings.avoidedCost: Reuse the exact1-minus-two-times-coefficient feedback for every channel instead of recalculating it in each low-pass sample.
findings.evidence: Shared crossover callers retain exact constructor/tick/reset behavior; a stereo tick computes one feedback scalar rather than two channel computations.
findings.limitations: Feedback follows the same smoothed coefficient, including constructor and reset. Configure changes only target until tick; no multiplication/addition regrouping.

findings.title: Prepare the fixed RMS detector complement
findings.avoidedCost: Reuse1-minus-detector across every per-frame compressor gain calculation.
findings.evidence: Each of the three multiband detectors avoids one fixed subtraction per frame; original multiplication/addition order and streamed/live telemetry fixture bytes are preserved.
findings.limitations: Only the fixed sample-rate detector complement is retained; attack/release smoothing complements remain dynamic.

findings.title: Retain unchanged compressor attack/release design
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid redesigning attack/release exponentials when updates change only thresholds, ratio or reduction controls.
findings.evidence: Red/green unrelated configure executes zero exp calls rather than two; changing one time constant executes one; neutral configure still clears reduction.
findings.limitations: Each time constant is invalidated independently via Object.is. Energy and reduction histories are retained, and every neutral-reset side effect still runs.

findings.title: Prepare linked band gain corrections once per frame
findings.avoidedCost: Calculate shared gain-minus-one once rather than once per output channel; the same cost is grouped once across deesser and multiband.
findings.evidence: Deesser stereo correction subtraction is one rather than two; multiband stores three corrections instead of recomputing six stereo corrections. Live and offline PCM/telemetry are exact.
findings.limitations: Shared multiband corrections retain Float64 precision; band addition order is unchanged. The two effect callsites count as one cost.

findings.title: Omit unconsumed offline multiband telemetry
findings.avoidedCost: Private offline construction omits input/output peak and minimum-gain reductions that the selection caller never reads.
findings.evidence: Red/green 2049-frame mono selection performs zero Math.abs calls instead of 4098; public live processor still performs 4098 and publishes the exact same analysis window.
findings.limitations: The exact selection caller returns only PCM. Public factory and worklet readAnalysis are unchanged; no published analysis is skipped and all input validation still executes.

findings.title: Use scalar linked powers instead of typed scratch
findings.avoidedCost: Remove per-frame three-element Float64 scratch clearing and indexed power updates/reads by retaining three local scalar maxima.
findings.evidence: The production multiband frame loop no longer allocates a power scratch array or calls its fill on each frame; channel maximum order remains exact in frozen mono/three-channel fixtures.
findings.limitations: Every band power and compressor still runs. Makeup and compression gain Float64 rounding and linked-channel max order are preserved.

findings.title: Prepare standard filter channel state strides
findings.avoidedCost: Hoist fixed channel-times-stage state addressing outside frame/stage loops.
findings.evidence: A stereo 48000-frame four-stage filter computes channel stride twice per block rather than 384000 stage iterations; exact multi-stage filters and parameter changes pass.
findings.limitations: Validated channel/stage sizes make all integer address arithmetic exact. Filter state equations and stage traversal are unchanged; grouped short timings may be within noise.

findings.title: Allocate standard-effect zero input only when needed
findings.avoidedCost: Zero-latency selections avoid a channel-sized set of unused1024-frame padding buffers.
findings.evidence: Red/green 2049-frame stereo filter has four Float32 allocations (two outputs/two scratch) rather than six; latency-bearing noise-gate parity still includes tail padding.
findings.limitations: Latency and partial flushes retain lazily owned zero buffers, explicit fill and source copy. Full input views remain synchronously borrowed; returned PCM is owned.

findings.title: Use full standard-effect output blocks directly
findings.avoidedCost: Avoid allocating a typed subarray wrapper for full scratch blocks copied into owned selection output.
findings.evidence: Red/green 2049-frame mono selection creates four total subarray views rather than six: three input views and only the final partial output view.
findings.limitations: Delayed or partial output windows still use exact subarray ranges; full copies include no stale tail and output ownership is unchanged.

findings.title: Prepare equal-endpoint Chirp frequency
findings.avoidedCost: For equal frequency and equal positive amplitude, prepare the original phase step once and avoid per-frame logarithmic exponentiation/frequency interpolation.
findings.evidence: Red/green 1040-frame constant Chirp executes zero frequency-ratio powers rather than 1040; changing endpoints retains1040. Separate prepared factory avoids the rejected common variable-path regression.
findings.limitations: Shared guard requires equal validated frequencies and equal positive amplitudes. Candidate 28 is a distinct amplitude computation in this same guarded path; no individual timing is attributed. Ordinary variable loop is original.

findings.title: Prepare equal positive-amplitude Chirp gain
findings.avoidedCost: For equal frequency and equal positive amplitude, avoid per-frame zero-difference amplitude interpolation.
findings.evidence: A separate red/green counter records zero amplitude interpolations rather than 1040 for the constant job, while variable endpoints retain 1040; all waveform/partition PCM hashes match.
findings.limitations: This shares candidate 27 guard but removes the independently executed amplitude multiply/add. Zero and signed-zero amplitudes keep original arithmetic. No per-item timing attribution; constant-frequency/varying-amplitude jobs retain the original path.

findings.title: Retain only the active DTMF symbol timing
findings.avoidedCost: Keep scalar active tone start/end until symbol advancement instead of recomputing scaled geometry for every partial block request.
findings.evidence: Red/green 100 one-frame requests within a scaled tone calculate geometry once rather than 100 times; natural/scaled, cached/uncached and irregular partitions preserve exact bytes.
findings.limitations: Only two scalar bounds are retained; no new PCM cache. Symbol advancement, final-tone rounding, silence and existing bounded tone cache behavior are unchanged.

findings.title: Prepare fixed DTMF and Morse angular prefixes
findings.avoidedCost: Hoist the original left-associated2-times-PI-times-frequency prefix from every keyed PCM frame.
findings.evidence: The long uncached DTMF loop computes two fixed angular prefixes per fill rather than two per frame; Morse computes one prefix per job. Both are grouped as one cost and all keyed PCM hashes match.
findings.limitations: Subsequent multiplication by local frame and division by sample rate remain in the original order. Existing cached DTMF benefit is unchanged; Morse/short workloads may be at host timing noise, with no guaranteed isolated speedup.
